body:
# Independent audit: uniform properness and total buffered force

Audited source: `candidate ed103e599726c87f`, Sections 1--7.

Also checked against the actual hypotheses of `candidate cebc39c4f5ccbc96` and the SAME-dual normalization in `candidate 1a7cfa3d1047cbae`, Sections 1--4.



The geometric conclusions apply to the compact globally minimizing or globally o(1)-optimal sequence covered by the vanishing theorem. The force and entropy conclusions additionally require the actual SAME physical/parameter separator. Near-optimal values alone do not provide that separator, and an unrelated parameter-only certificate cannot replace it.

## 1. Uniform geometric consequences

The body-limit dependency now explicitly assumes the selected minimal-bad-base compactness and limiting closed-minor quota framework. Badness on an arbitrary fixed base is not used as a substitute. Its conclusion is uniform vanishing of epsilon^(d+1)L on sampled fibers and hence of the physical scalar displacement. Bounded bodies, positive masses, and positive definite covariance therefore give the constants used in the present source.

The all-normal slab bound is uniform in the base tilt. For Euclidean unit continuous normal, the physical threshold increase is at most delta_max sqrt(lambda_+), while the sum of section areas is at most A. This gives the source's S_max delta_max bound with S_max=A sqrt(lambda_+). Pure-base cap masses do not change at all. The phrase about increasing thresholds means increasing the buffer displacement, which lowers the defining cap threshold and increases captured mass.

At a deepest mark, combine this bound with the independently audited inequality

    ordinaryDepth(p,y) <= baseDepth(p)-V_p/2.

It follows that baseDepth(p)-Q >= V_p/2-S_max delta_max. For all sufficiently small epsilon this is at least v/4, uniformly at every deepest base. The rank-zero convention baseDepth=M is harmless: it is only a formal comparison value and introduces no new nonzero pure-base normal.

The uniform own-interiority can also be seen directly. A common own ball gives a uniform positive lower bound on the maximal raw depth. Slab comparison then bounds the ordinary depth at every buffered maximizer below by a common positive number. Ordinary depth is zero at sampled own-boundary points, using the finite support-height roof, and it is uniformly Lipschitz within each fiber. Thus all such maximizers stay a uniform positive distance from the own boundary. This argument uses neither a critical menu nor a martingale.

For Gamma(u)=1, the bounds

    1/sqrt(lambda_+) <= ||u|| <= 1/sqrt(lambda_-)

have the correct directions. The shifted own plane is within delta_max sqrt(lambda_+) of the source. It therefore crosses a fixed own ball in a section of radius at least sqrt(3)r/2. Dividing the section area by ||u|| gives exactly the stated S_min. This proves properness for EVERY nonvertical buffered through-source plane, independently of its base tilt or optimality. For d=1 the own section has H_0 measure one and the same coarea calculation applies.

Every effective total coarea includes that unambiguous proper own contribution, and all other proper/inside/outside contributions are bounded by the sum of maximal sections with selectors in [0,1]. Hence S_min <= T_j <= S_max is valid even when other fibers have supporting facets. The source does not incorrectly infer that those other supporting facets disappear.

## 2. Same-separator coefficients, including nonfinite selector mixtures

The source retains the actual finite-contact continuation and physical-cone hypotheses of its nonregular dual dependency. Under them,

    B_ib=sum_j rho_ij/T_ijb,
    kappa_ia=sum_b lambda_iab/B_ib,
    e_ia=epsilon f_ia kappa_ia,
    Delta=sum_ia e_ia

are precisely the previously audited coefficients. In the new proper-only regime the common dual weights sum to one over these groups. Thus the harmonic inequalities give S_min <= K=sum_ia kappa_ia <= S_max. There is no missing coarea, source-count, or normalization factor.

The bound also has a direct aggregate proof, avoiding any unnecessary assumption that the full compact-selector common dual is represented by finitely many branches. The audited effective equations are

    omega_ij T_ij=kappa_i rho_ij,
    sum_j rho_ij=1,
    sum_j omega_ij=eta_i.

Summing the first equation gives

    kappa_i=sum_j omega_ij T_ij,
    S_min eta_i<=kappa_i<=S_max eta_i.

Then sum_i eta_i=1 gives the same bounds. This applies directly to the weak-star compact common dual for the whole physically addable test class. It also shows that only the cap coarea data from that dual are being used; there is no identification of its allocated surface measure with a volume row.

Repeated occurrences of a mark can be merged because L, E, and delta agree at that mark. Adding their kappa and the corresponding sigma-weighted rows preserves every displayed identity. Discarding zero kappa leaves positive w and sigma on the same finite contact index set. Own-interiority and positive L give E_a>0 and delta_a>0, hence Delta>0.

## 3. Exact entropy calculation

The essential hypothesis is that the parameter component of this SAME separator gives the contact probabilities rho_a with

    E_rho_a L=L_a,
    sum_a (sigma_a/L_a)rho_a=dm/(M L),
    sigma_a=kappa_a delta_a/Delta.

Then d bar_rho_a=(L/L_a)d rho_a is a probability, and its sigma mixture is EXACT original normalized volume dm/M. Therefore

    sum_a sigma_a KL(bar_rho_a || rho_a)
      = (1/M) integral log L dm - sum_a sigma_a log L_a
      = -sum_a sigma_a log L_a = K_V>=0.

The direction of relative entropy is correct. It is the original-volume row relative to the tilted row, not its reverse. At the stated positive continuous finite-parameter pairs all logarithms are bounded; more generally the identity needs the retained logarithmic integrability. No limiting exchange of divergent reciprocals is used.

With N=d+1 and delta_a=epsilon(L_a E_a/M)^(1/N), this gives

    sum_a sigma_a log delta_a
      =log epsilon-[K_V+sum_a sigma_a log(M/E_a)]/N.

Since w_a=kappa_a/K,

    sigma_a/w_a=delta_a/(Delta/K),
    KL(sigma||w)=sum_a sigma_a log delta_a-log(Delta/K).

Subtracting gives exactly

    log(epsilon K/Delta)
      =KL(sigma||w)+[K_V+sum_a sigma_a log(M/E_a)]/N.

All three terms on the right are nonnegative: the two relative entropies, and the energy-volume term because 0<E_a<=V_(p_a)<=M. Thus Delta<=epsilon K<=epsilon S_max. This bound is not a pointwise claim that any delta_a<=epsilon or L_a<=1. It does not imply a matching lower bound on Delta.

For I=log(epsilon K/Delta), the identity Delta=epsilon K exp(-I) and I exp(-I)<=1/e give every bound in (15), including the factor N multiplying Delta K_V. The unscaled entropies can diverge. The statement makes no conclusion about an independently defined surface logarithmic reserve, and correctly warns that Delta=O(epsilon) is insufficient to discard an uncontrolled pointwise term Delta log L.

## 4. A slightly broader upper-bound scope

The displayed theorem is sound in its stated uniform-properness setting. One can separate which hypotheses are needed for which conclusion.

The exact entropy identity and Delta<=epsilon K need only the SAME-row normalization, energy-volume bound, and positive Delta. Uniform vanishing is not used in their algebra. Moreover, whenever the mixed atomic/proper common separator from the audited dependency is available, its aggregate equations give

    K<=S_max sum_(proper i) eta_i<=S_max

even if atomic weights remain. Hence the upper O(epsilon) force bound already applies in that broader bounded-geometry setting, provided the mixed construction establishes Delta>0 and its exact same-separator volume rows. The new uniform geometric theorem is needed for the lower K>=S_min, the uniform atomic gap, and the properness of ALL own through-source directions. This observation does not supply the missing separator at arbitrary near-optimal pairs and does not remove its actual-path hypotheses.

## 5. Actual sharp interval calibration

For [-1,1], the projective energy is E(y)=2(1-y^2), M=2, and Sigma=1/3. At y=0 the two Gamma-normalized normals have coarea 1/sqrt(3), so B=sqrt(3) and K=1/sqrt(3). With L=1, delta=epsilon and Delta=epsilon/sqrt(3)=epsilon K. Both relative entropies and log(M/E) vanish.

For an arbitrary positive concave log-normalized U on this interval, log U is concave and Jensen gives U(0)>=1. The buffered depth at zero is therefore at least the value for L=1, including the case when the larger displacement saturates the interval. For L=1 the raw depth is

    1-|y|+(epsilon/sqrt(3))sqrt(1-y^2),

and, for 0<epsilon<1, its smaller cap is never full and its unique maximum is at zero. Thus the claimed global parameter optimum is actual. Affine invariance makes all intervals equivalent in this one-fiber setting, so it is also an actual joint interval/body optimum. This is a safe calibration, not an example in the hypothetical bad class, and the source says so.

The result leaves cap payment and the control of the surface part of the response unresolved. It is a rigorously normalized scale and volume-entropy bound.
